subject: Oceanography
title: Arctic Water Masses
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Arctic Water Masses.

hook.text: The Arctic Ocean has a layered structure—cold fresh water on top, warm salty Atlantic water trapped below.

buildup.text: River runoff and ice melt create a fresh surface layer—lighter than the salty layers beneath.

discovery.text: Warm Atlantic water flows in at depth through Fram Strait—carrying heat that could melt ice from below.

twist.text: A cold halocline separates these layers—preventing warm water from reaching the ice. If it weakens, ice melts faster.

climax.text: Climate change is weakening this barrier—warm Atlantic water is getting closer to the surface ice.

punchline.text: A thin layer of cold water is all that protects Arctic ice from warm intruders.

quiz.question: What protects Arctic sea ice from warm Atlantic water below?
options: Ocean currents pushing warm water away
